industry.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
industry.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration ( MMX ) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).

industry.title: BUILDING THE WORLD’S MOST ADVANCED MOBILE NETWORK
industry.summary: This week marked two major milestones for Starlink Mobile. SpaceX announced an agreement to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio of up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band. This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US.

industry.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
industry.summary: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.

papers.title: Wavelet-Enhanced Feature Pyramid Network for Pose Estimation of Non-Cooperative Spacecraft
papers.summary: Monocular six-degree-of-freedom pose estimation of non-cooperative spacecraft is critical for a variety of on-orbit missions. However, it remains a challenging task due to extreme illumination variations, pronounced scale differences, complex rotational motions, and the sparse geometric characteristics of spacecraft.

papers.title: Restricted Three-Body Problem Fixed-Point Identification via High-Order Transfer Maps
papers.summary: Periodic orbits (POs) play a central role in the circular restricted three-body problem (CRTBP). This paper presents a framework for identifying single- and multirevolution POs by searching for fixed points of selected Poincaré maps of the CRTBP.
papers.source: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Disbond Growth in Sandwich Panels Under Pressurization and Compression
papers.summary: Honeycomb-core sandwich structures are increasingly used in aircraft, making disbond propagation driven by ground–air–ground (GAG) pressurization cycles a significant safety concern. Because this mechanism involves coupled structural, thermodynamic, and fracture processes, its behavior remains insufficiently understood.

Beyond classical similitude: group theoretic extrapolation of hypersonic stagnation-point boundary layers
papers.summary: Motivated by the need to extrapolate the results from ground-based experiments to the conditions of high-speed flight, we present the Lie equivalence-symmetry analysis of the hypersonic stagnation-point boundary layers (BLs). We demonstrate the application of the equivalence symmetry on the set of coupled ordinary differential equations (ODEs) which are physically relevant in hypersonics.

papers.title: Propagation and absorption of sound in a waveguide with side-wall impedance gradient
papers.summary: Over the past two decades, acoustic retarding structures, analogised to sonic ‘black holes’ (SBH), have garnered significant attention for their potential to achieve perfect sound absorption. Typical designs feature annular rings with progressively smaller radii designed to bring sound waves to rest at zero radius.

papers.title: Influencing factors and physical mechanism of rheological evolution of oil-based complex fluids at ultralow temperatures
papers.summary: Extreme low-temperature environments pose significant challenges to fluid physics. It is urgent to maintain good rheological behavior of oil-based complex fluids under extreme, low-temperature conditions.

papers.title: The weakly nonlinear admittance at open ends of two- and three-dimensional acoustic waveguides
papers.summary: We formulate a weakly nonlinear exit condition for open ends of acoustic waveguides; to our knowledge, this is the first time a general acoustic open end has been analysed outside the linear regime. The formulation neglects mean flow, vortex separation and viscous effects.
